ratings.reasons: All six lines move 1.3 toward the camera, so on a phone it reads as a zoom, not a general with troops falling in; by frame 230 the left halves are cut off the left edge of the frame. The general is never singled out, since every line does the same thing.
ratings.redo: Keep depth fixed and make the general different from the troops: the five yin lines' halves drift loose (each half a small, different sideways offset, dimmed), then line 2 brightens once and the yin lines slide back into straight ranks one at a time, nearest first, each brightening as it aligns. It ends on 7, ordered around the one strong line: many people held in order by one correct leader.

ratings.reasons: The idea is right (heaven below rising, earth above sinking, they meet), but the move is only half the gap between the trigrams, so start and end stills look almost the same, and closing the gap blurs the two trigrams a newcomer should learn.
ratings.redo: Make it larger and make the meeting the event: the lower three rise and the upper three sink until lines 3 and 4 touch, a single amber flash runs along the seam (bite.py's flash), then both trigrams ease back to their places while the seam cools. Use the same distance as 12's drift in the other direction, so 11 and 12 read as a pair.

ratings.reasons: Clear at a glance: the gap between heaven and earth widens by about 1.2 and both trigrams dim, which is the Tuan's 'heaven and earth do not interact'. It needs only one move and adds nothing.

The one yang line recedes and dims until it is visibly smaller than the yin lines around it, so 'the one with most to show keeps low' comes across, and the mountain-under-earth trigrams stay intact. The middle of the move is gentle, but the end state is unmistakable.

The bottom line splits, dims and slides apart, leaving six yin, then comes back whole with an amber flash: 'the light returns at the bottom' reads plainly and the first line stays the focus. The halves drift a little past the yin lines' edges, which is fine.

The whole hexagram squashes 28% toward its middle and expands again, which reads as a squeeze or breath, not a mouth. It also repeats what bite.py did with the jaws and misses the trigram reading, thunder moving below and mountain still above.
ratings.redo: Move only the lower jaw: the top yang line (mountain, still) stays put; the bottom yang line (thunder, moving) rises slowly, pushing the lower two yin lines up before it, stops short of the upper trigram, and lowers again, twice at a calm pace. It shows the lower jaw working and the upper holding, and it gives the lesson a hook: watch what goes in and what comes out.

ratings.reasons: The yin ends tilting read, but since the top and bottom pairs both drop at their outer ends, the stack looks like two little roofs or drooping wings, not a beam overloaded in the middle. The four yang lines' 0.15 drop cannot be seen, so the cause (too much weight in the middle) is missing.
ratings.redo: Show the load and then the strain: the four yang lines brighten and spread slightly apart (the middle grows), and the weak ends bend away from them, the top pair's outer ends lifting and the bottom pair's outer ends dropping (about 12 degrees), so the whole figure bulges like a bundle too thick for its ties. Hold at the strain.

ratings.reasons: The two yin centres turning amber is clean and visible, but it is a static colour change: it says 'hollow middle' without saying anything about clinging or brightness, and a newcomer sees two lines change colour.
ratings.redo: Use the Great Image, brightness doubled and carried on: the lower yin centre warms to amber, then the amber spreads to the yang lines above and below it (the flame taking hold of what it clings to), then passes up to the upper trigram's centre, which lights and spreads the same way. Then all fade back to green except the two centres. Two identical flames one after the other also teaches the doubled trigram.

ratings.reasons: The top yin's halves slide apart and fade, leaving five yang with the top empty: 'the strong resolutely remove the one weak line' is clear. The glow climbing the five lines is too faint to read on a phone; it should be brighter so the five act together before the top goes, but this is polish.

The crack is 0.18 wide and the yin lift 0.14, so in frame 116 it is a hairline a phone viewer will not see; the metal-brake reference cannot be followed without text. The idea that one small yin arrives under five yang and must be checked early is lost.
ratings.redo: The lone yin at the bottom brightens and rises clearly (0.4 or more) toward line 2; line 2 flashes amber as it arrives (line 2 holds it, 'a fish in the bag') and the yin settles back to its place and dims. No crack. It shows a small beginning met and contained by the line next to it.

ratings.reasons: Jolting lines break the calm-motion rule (no punch or shake), and in frame 59 the jolted fourth line rides up into the yin line above it, so the lines overlap. The lesson (shock comes, the composed man keeps his ladle and examines himself) is not in a jump.
ratings.redo: Make the shock light, not movement: an amber flash starts in line 1 and runs up through each line in turn, then a second, fainter one starts in line 4 and runs up the upper trigram. Every line stays exactly where it is and the hexagram is still at the end, so the thunder passes and the lines do not move.

ratings.reasons: The empty heart opening in the middle reads well and is the core image of the hexagram. But at 0.8 each way the outer halves leave the frame (truth-72 cuts the left halves and nearly the right), so it looks like a crop error on a phone.
ratings.redo: Same move, smaller, about 0.45 each way, so all four halves stay inside the frame, and hold the opening a beat longer before it closes. Optionally brighten lines 2 and 5 while it is open (firm at the centres, empty within), which is the Tuan's reading, and nothing more.
